name: Galderma
desc: Dermatology company selling injectable aesthetics, consumer skincare such as Cetaphil, and prescription skin treatments worldwide.
markets: Sells in about 90 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific through doctors, pharmacies and retailers.
rationale: Global skincare and aesthetics brands such as Cetaphil and Restylane could use F1 for premium consumer reach and clinician hospitality.
changed: Taken private by EQT-led consortium in 2019; IPO on SIX Swiss Exchange in 2024

name: THG
desc: Online retail and brand group selling beauty products through LookFantastic and Cult Beauty and sports nutrition through Myprotein.
markets: Sells online to consumers in many countries, with the UK, Europe, US and Asia as main markets.
rationale: Myprotein sports nutrition and global online beauty sites suit F1's young international fan base and performance messaging.
changed: Separated its THG Ingenuity technology business in 2025

name: dsm-firmenich
desc: Supplier of flavours, fragrances, vitamins and nutrition ingredients to food, beverage, personal care and pharma manufacturers.
markets: Serves manufacturers worldwide across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific; animal nutrition business being divested.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier with little consumer visibility; F1 value limited to hospitality and sustainability messaging.
changed: Formed by merger of DSM and Firmenich in 2023; agreed sale of animal nutrition and health unit in 2025

name: Valentino
desc: Italian luxury fashion house selling ready-to-wear, leather goods, shoes and accessories through boutiques and wholesale worldwide.
markets: Sells through its own boutiques, department stores and online across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Globally recognised luxury brand whose clientele overlaps with F1 paddock and Grand Prix hospitality audiences.
changed: Kering agreed in 2023 to buy a 30 percent stake, with an option on the rest

name: Debenhams Group
desc: Online fashion and beauty retailer operating Debenhams.com, boohoo, boohooMAN, PrettyLittleThing and Karen Millen brands.
markets: Main market is the UK, with online sales to consumers in the US, Europe and Australia.
rationale: UK-centred online retailer; F1 British Grand Prix or youth fashion tie-ins plausible, though finances are stretched.
changed: boohoo group plc renamed Debenhams Group in 2025

name: Nykaa
desc: Indian retailer selling beauty, personal care and fashion products online and through its own physical stores.
markets: Customers mainly in India; has a beauty retail joint venture in the Gulf region.
rationale: Strong Indian consumer brand; F1 could reach affluent young Indians, though F1 has no race in India.

name: Wella Company
desc: Hair and nail care company selling Wella Professionals, Clairol, OPI, Nioxin and ghd products to salons and retailers.
markets: Sells to salons, retailers and consumers in over 100 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Global beauty brands like ghd and OPI could use F1 for consumer marketing and salon partner hospitality.
changed: Coty sold a majority stake to KKR in 2020

name: Bath & Body Works
desc: Specialty retailer of body care, fragrance mists, soaps and scented candles through its own stores and online.
industry: body care and home fragrance retail
markets: Mainly US and Canada company-run stores, plus franchised international stores in the Middle East and elsewhere.
rationale: Very strong North American consumer brand; US Grand Prix tie-ins plausible, though audience skews female mall shoppers.
changed: Spun off from L Brands in 2021

name: BBB Foods (Tiendas 3B)
desc: Hard-discount grocery chain selling food, household cleaning and personal hygiene products through Tiendas 3B neighbourhood stores.
markets: Stores in Mexico only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic discount grocer with value-focused shoppers; Mexico City Grand Prix is a possible but weak fit.
changed: Parent BBB Foods listed on the NYSE in 2024

name: Growve
desc: Brand aggregator that acquires and grows consumer brands in beauty and personal care, mainly sold online.
markets: Customers believed to be mainly US online shoppers; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Portfolio of small online brands with no single household name; weak F1 fit.

name: Yatsen Holding
desc: Chinese beauty group selling Perfect Diary cosmetics and skincare brands such as Galenic and DR.WU, mainly online.
markets: Customers mainly in mainland China, with smaller sales of acquired skincare brands abroad.
rationale: Chinese consumer beauty brand; F1 Shanghai Grand Prix could fit, but revenue pressure limits budgets.

name: Glossier
desc: Beauty brand selling skincare and make-up products online, in its own stores and through Sephora.
markets: Main markets are the US, Canada and UK, plus retail partners such as Sephora, Space NK and Mecca.
rationale: Community-driven beauty brand for young women; F1's growing female audience gives a plausible but niche fit.

name: Revlon
desc: Cosmetics company selling make-up, nail, hair colour and fragrance brands including Revlon, Almay and Elizabeth Arden.
markets: Products sold in about 150 countries through mass retailers and pharmacies.
rationale: Well-known global beauty brand rebuilding after bankruptcy; F1 could target its growing female audience.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2022 and emerged in 2023 owned by its former lenders

name: Madison Reed
desc: Hair colour brand selling at-home colour kits online and through retailers, plus its own Hair Color Bar salons.
markets: Customers in the US through online subscription, retailers and its own salons; no verified international plans.
rationale: US-only beauty brand with female target audience; weak F1 fit beyond a US race.

name: Natura Cosméticos
desc: Cosmetics group selling Natura and Avon beauty, fragrance and personal care products, largely through direct-selling consultants.
markets: Mainly Latin America, with Avon operations in other regions; Aesop and The Body Shop already sold.
rationale: Strong Latin American consumer brands; São Paulo and Mexico Grand Prix give a plausible regional fit.
changed: Sold Aesop to L'Oréal and The Body Shop to Aurelius in 2023; Avon Products filed for Chapter 11 in 2024

name: Venus Concept
desc: Maker of energy-based aesthetic devices for body contouring, skin treatments and hair restoration sold to clinics.
markets: Sells to aesthetic clinics in North America and other countries through direct sales and distributors.
rationale: Small B2B device maker with no consumer brand and tight finances; weak F1 fit.

name: Ulta Beauty
desc: Beauty retailer selling cosmetics, skincare, haircare and fragrance plus salon services through stores and online.
markets: Mainly US stores; entered Mexico through a partnership in 2025 and plans Middle East stores via franchise.
rationale: Largest US beauty retailer; US Grand Prix events and F1's female fan growth give a plausible fit.

name: Grupo Cimed
desc: Brazilian pharmaceutical company making generic medicines, over-the-counter products, vitamins and cosmetics sold through pharmacies.
markets: Customers mainly in Brazil through pharmacy chains; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Heavy advertiser in Brazil; São Paulo Grand Prix links plausible, but domestic focus limits global value.

name: AptarGroup
desc: Maker of dispensing pumps, sprays, closures and drug delivery devices for beauty, pharma, food and home care brands.
markets: Manufacturing in about 18 countries, serving customers across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier with no consumer brand; F1 value limited to client hospitality.

name: European Wax Center
desc: Franchisor of waxing salons offering hair removal services and selling its own skincare products in the US.
markets: Over 1,000 centres in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-only personal care franchise with a mainly female clientele; weak F1 fit.

name: Regis Corporation
desc: Franchisor of hair salons under brands including Supercuts, SmartStyle and Cost Cutters, mainly in North America.
markets: Salons mainly in the US, with some in Canada and other markets through franchisees.
rationale: Mass-market North American salon franchisor with a limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit beyond local US promotions.

name: Sono Bello
desc: Cosmetic surgery provider performing laser liposuction and body contouring procedures through a network of US centres.
markets: Patients in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-only elective surgery provider; cosmetic surgery is a sensitive sponsorship category, weak F1 fit.

name: Lindex Group
desc: Fashion retailer selling women's wear, lingerie, children's clothing and beauty products through Lindex stores and online.
markets: Mainly Nordic countries and the Baltics, with stores in some other European markets and franchise partners.
rationale: Nordic consumer fashion brand with mainly female shoppers; limited F1 fit outside Scandinavian marketing activity.
changed: Stockmann plc renamed Lindex Group in 2024; Stockmann department stores divested

name: Lush Fresh Handmade Cosmetics
desc: Retailer and maker of handmade cosmetics such as bath bombs, soaps and skincare sold in its own shops.
markets: Around 900 shops in about 50 countries across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Strong ethical brand, but anti-advertising culture and environmental stance make F1 a poor fit.

name: Thrive Market
desc: Membership-based online retailer selling organic and natural groceries, household goods and beauty products to US members.
markets: Members in the US only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: US-only online grocer focused on health-conscious households; little reason to use a global motorsport platform, weak fit.

name: Moody's Corporation
desc: Provides credit ratings, research, data and risk analytics software to investors, banks, companies and governments.
markets: Operates across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global B2B brand serving finance clients; F1 hospitality and data-analytics showcase could fit like rival financial-data sponsors.

name: MAV Beauty Brands
desc: Personal care company selling hair care brands such as Marc Anthony and Renpure through retailers and online.
markets: Products sold mainly through retailers in the US and Canada; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Mass-market hair care brands with limited marketing budgets and a North American focus; weak F1 fit.
changed: Delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange in 2023 after a lender-led recapitalisation

name: Pacific World Corporation
desc: Supplier of beauty and personal care products to retailers; brands and current ownership not confirmed.
markets: Customers assumed to be US retailers; no verified international activity.
rationale: Little-known supplier with unconfirmed brands, ownership and status; weak F1 fit until verified it still operates.

name: JCPenney
desc: Department store chain selling apparel, home goods, beauty and jewellery through about 650 US stores and online.
markets: Customers in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Mid-market domestic retailer under cost pressure; weak F1 fit beyond US race marketing.
changed: Emerged from 2020 bankruptcy owned by Simon and Brookfield; combined into Catalyst Brands in 2025

name: Hudson's Bay Company
desc: Former Canadian department store group that liquidated its stores in 2025; brand rights now held elsewhere.
markets: No operations; Canadian stores closed in 2025 and brand intellectual property sold to Canadian Tire.
rationale: Defunct retailer whose stores closed in 2025 and whose brand now belongs to Canadian Tire; no F1 fit.
changed: Liquidated in 2025; brand and intellectual property bought by Canadian Tire

name: Gildan Activewear
desc: Makes basic apparel such as T-shirts, fleece, socks and underwear under Gildan, Comfort Colors and Gold Toe brands.
markets: Sells mainly in North America to screen printers, distributors and retailers, with sales in Europe and Asia.
rationale: Mostly wholesale blank apparel with modest consumer brand; F1 fit limited to merchandise supply.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to acquire HanesBrands

name: Aritzia
desc: Women's fashion retailer designing and selling everyday luxury apparel under its own labels through boutiques and online.
markets: Boutiques and e-commerce in Canada and the United States; US is the main growth market.
rationale: Strong North American fashion brand targeting young women; F1's female audience growth gives a plausible fit.

name: Transitions Optical
desc: Makes photochromic spectacle lenses that darken in sunlight, sold through eyewear retailers and eye-care professionals.
markets: Lenses sold through opticians and lens makers across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Eyewear technology brand within a group already active in F1; performance-vision messaging fits.
changed: Wholly owned by Essilor from 2014; part of EssilorLuxottica since 2018
f1: Parent EssilorLuxottica's Ray-Ban and Oakley brands are current F1 team partners

name: Miniso
desc: Variety retailer selling low-cost household goods, cosmetics, toys and licensed IP products through franchised stores.
markets: Over 7,000 stores in about 100 countries across Asia, the Americas, Europe and the Middle East.
rationale: Mass-market youth retail brand with IP collaborations; F1 licensed merchandise or China activation plausible.

name: Rent the Runway
desc: Online platform renting designer clothing and accessories to women by subscription or single order, with some resale.
markets: Customers in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Niche US fashion rental service with tight finances and no international customers; weak F1 fit.

name: VF Corporation
desc: Apparel and footwear company owning The North Face, Vans, Timberland, Kipling and Eastpak, sold through wholesale and stores.
markets: Sells in about 100 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global consumer brands such as The North Face and Vans could use F1 for lifestyle reach.
changed: Sold Supreme to EssilorLuxottica in 2024 and Dickies to Bluestar Alliance in 2025

name: Warby Parker
desc: Eyewear company selling prescription glasses, sunglasses and contact lenses through its own stores and online, plus eye exams.
markets: Stores and online sales in the US and Canada; no verified wider expansion.
rationale: US and Canadian direct-to-consumer eyewear brand; limited F1 fit outside North American race marketing.

name: Coupang
desc: E-commerce company running a fast-delivery online marketplace, food delivery and streaming service, mainly in South Korea.
markets: Operates mainly in South Korea and Taiwan; owns global luxury marketplace Farfetch.
rationale: Dominant Korean consumer brand; F1 could support Farfetch luxury positioning and Asian growth, moderate fit.
changed: Acquired Farfetch in 2024

name: Nordstrom
desc: Department store chain selling fashion, shoes, beauty and home goods through Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack stores and online.
markets: Stores in the US; closed its Canadian stores in 2023.
rationale: Upmarket US retailer; US Grand Prix hospitality plausible but domestic focus limits F1 value.
changed: Taken private in 2025 by the Nordstrom family and El Puerto de Liverpool

name: BVI Medical
desc: Makes ophthalmic surgical devices, including cataract and retina instruments, intraocular lenses and glaucoma products, for surgeons.
markets: Sells to eye surgeons and hospitals in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B surgical device maker with no consumer visibility and a narrow clinical audience; weak F1 fit.

name: Ermenegildo Zegna Group
desc: Luxury group making menswear and tailoring under Zegna and Tom Ford Fashion and selling Thom Browne collections.
markets: Sells through its own stores, wholesale and online across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Luxury menswear clientele overlaps with F1 paddock audiences; strong hospitality and premium brand fit.
changed: Listed on the NYSE in 2021 through a SPAC merger

name: Canada Goose
desc: Designs and sells luxury cold-weather down jackets, apparel and footwear through its own stores, online and wholesale.
markets: Sells in more than 50 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Premium outerwear brand with global reach; possible F1 team or Canadian Grand Prix tie-in.

name: Farfetch
desc: Online luxury fashion marketplace selling products from boutiques and brands, plus Browns stores and New Guards brands.
markets: Sells to consumers in about 190 countries worldwide.
rationale: Global luxury marketplace whose affluent shoppers overlap with F1 audiences; strong fit if budgets allow.
changed: Acquired by Coupang in 2024 and delisted from the NYSE

name: Dolce & Gabbana
desc: Italian luxury fashion house selling ready-to-wear, couture, handbags, accessories, cosmetics and fragrances worldwide.
markets: Boutiques and wholesale across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Highly recognised luxury brand suited to F1 glamour and premium hospitality in Monaco, Miami or the Gulf.

name: Reformation
desc: Women's fashion brand selling dresses, tops, denim and shoes through its own stores and online.
markets: Main market is the US, with stores in Canada and the UK and online international sales.
rationale: Sustainability-led fashion brand for young women; weak F1 fit given environmental positioning.
changed: Permira acquired a majority stake in 2019

name: GOAT Group
desc: Online marketplace for authenticated new and used sneakers, apparel and accessories, plus Flight Club stores.
markets: Members worldwide across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Sneaker culture brand with young fans; F1 merchandise and drop collaborations plausible.

name: Mulberry Group
desc: British luxury brand making leather handbags, accessories and clothing, sold through its own stores, online and wholesale.
markets: Mainly the UK, with stores and partners in Europe and Asia.
rationale: British luxury brand with a premium clientele; British Grand Prix tie-in plausible but finances are tight.

name: Rothy's
desc: Footwear and accessories brand selling washable shoes and bags knitted from recycled plastic, online and in its stores.
markets: Customers mainly in the US through its website and stores.
rationale: US direct-to-consumer shoe brand with a sustainability image and female audience; weak F1 fit.

name: Alo Yoga
desc: Activewear brand selling yoga clothing, athleisure, footwear and wellness products through its own stores and online.
markets: Main market is the US, with stores in Asia, Europe and the Middle East and growing international e-commerce.
rationale: Fast-growing premium lifestyle brand whose wellness image and celebrity marketing could suit F1's young, affluent fan base.

name: Patagonia
desc: Outdoor clothing and equipment company selling jackets, fleece and gear through its own stores, retailers and online.
markets: Stores in more than ten countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, plus worldwide retail partners.
rationale: Environmental activist brand that avoids motorsport-style marketing and fossil-fuel associations; F1 partnership very unlikely.
changed: Ownership transferred to the Patagonia Purpose Trust and Holdfast Collective in 2022

name: RxSight
desc: Maker of the Light Adjustable Lens, an intraocular lens for cataract surgery adjusted after implantation with light treatment.
markets: Sales mainly to US ophthalmologists and surgery centres, with limited international sales.
rationale: B2B eye-surgery device maker selling to surgeons, with no consumer brand to promote; weak F1 fit.

name: Bombas
desc: Apparel brand selling socks, underwear, t-shirts and slippers mainly online, donating an item for every item sold.
markets: Customers mainly in the US through its website and some wholesale partners; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US comfort-apparel brand with a charity model; limited F1 fit beyond US race marketing.

name: Versace
desc: Italian luxury fashion house selling ready-to-wear, couture, accessories, fragrances and home products through boutiques worldwide.
markets: Sells through boutiques, department stores and online across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Globally known luxury brand suited to F1 glamour, paddock hospitality and Grand Prix events such as Monaco.
changed: Owned by Capri Holdings from 2018; acquired by Prada Group in 2025

name: Bira 91
desc: Craft beer brand selling wheat ales, lagers and other beers through retailers, bars and taprooms in India.
markets: Customers mainly in India, with limited exports; recent financial strain and funding difficulties.
rationale: Youth-focused Indian beer brand, but financial distress and alcohol rules limit F1 spending; weak fit.

name: Gong cha
desc: Bubble tea franchise selling milk teas, fruit teas and toppings through franchised and company-run shops worldwide.
markets: Shops in Asia, Australia, the Americas, Europe and the Middle East through franchise partners.
rationale: Youth-oriented beverage brand present in many F1 host markets; plausible fan engagement and activation fit.
changed: Acquired by TA Associates in 2019

name: Sula Vineyards
desc: Wine producer making Sula, Rasa and Dindori wines and running vineyard resorts and tasting rooms in India.
markets: Customers mainly in India, with exports to over 20 countries.
rationale: Leading Indian wine brand; premium lifestyle fit, but India-focused sales and alcohol ad rules limit F1 value.

name: C&C Group
desc: Makes and distributes cider and beer such as Magners, Bulmers and Tennent's, and supplies pubs in Britain and Ireland.
industry: cider and beer maker and distributor
markets: Mainly UK and Ireland, with Magners exported to other markets.
rationale: UK and Irish drinks group; British Grand Prix hospitality plausible but limited international scale.

name: Barry Callebaut
desc: Makes chocolate and cocoa products for food manufacturers, chocolatiers, bakeries and restaurants under Callebaut and Cacao Barry.
markets: Around 60 production sites in Europe, Africa, the Americas and Asia serving customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B chocolate supplier with little consumer visibility; F1 value limited to client hospitality.

name: Chobani
desc: Food company making Greek yogurt, oat milk, coffee creamers and La Colombe coffee drinks sold through grocery retailers.
markets: Mainly the US, with operations in Australia and sales in other export markets.
rationale: Strong US consumer brand with sports sponsorship experience; US Grand Prix events plausible.
changed: Agreed to acquire La Colombe coffee in 2023

name: JBS
desc: Meat processor selling beef, pork, chicken and prepared foods under brands such as Friboi, Seara, Swift and Pilgrim's.
markets: Operations in Brazil, the US, Australia, Europe and elsewhere, selling to customers in about 190 countries.
rationale: Huge food group with consumer brands in many markets; F1 plausible for Brazilian and global B2B visibility.
changed: Listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 2025

name: ofi (Olam Food Ingredients)
desc: Supplies cocoa, coffee, dairy, nuts and spice ingredients to food and beverage manufacturers and retailers worldwide.
markets: Sourcing and processing operations across Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas, serving manufacturers worldwide.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier with no consumer brand; F1 value limited to hospitality.

name: Guala Closures Group
desc: Makes aluminium and plastic closures for spirits, wine, water and beverage bottles, including tamper-evident and anti-counterfeit caps.
markets: Plants in many countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia, Africa and Australia, serving global drinks groups.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier with no consumer awareness; weak F1 fit beyond hospitality for drinks clients.
changed: Taken private by Investindustrial in 2021

name: Haldiram Snacks
desc: Indian snack maker selling Haldiram's namkeen, bhujia, sweets and ready-to-eat foods through retailers and its restaurants.
markets: Mainly India, with exports to many countries, particularly those with Indian diaspora communities.
rationale: Beloved Indian consumer brand with large ad budgets; F1 could support its overseas and premium growth.
changed: Temasek, ADIA and Alpha Wave bought minority stakes in 2025

name: The Hershey Company
desc: Confectionery and snack company making Hershey's, Reese's, Kisses, Jolly Rancher and SkinnyPop products for retailers.
markets: Most sales in North America, with smaller operations in Latin America, Asia and other export markets.
rationale: Household US snack brand; US Grand Prix events and fan sampling activations give a plausible but not obvious fit.
f1: Makes KitKat in the US under licence from Nestlé, whose KitKat brand is an F1 partner

name: JDE Peet's
desc: Coffee and tea company selling Jacobs, Douwe Egberts, L'OR, Tassimo, Senseo and Peet's to retailers and foodservice.
markets: Sells in more than 100 markets across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Global coffee brands like L'OR suit F1 hospitality and premium consumer activation.
changed: Keurig Dr Pepper agreed in 2025 to acquire it; completion not confirmed

name: Jersey Mike's Subs
desc: Franchisor of sub sandwich restaurants with about 3,000 locations serving sandwiches in-store and online.
markets: Restaurants mainly in the US, plus Canada; no verified wider expansion.
rationale: US restaurant brand already active in motorsport sponsorship; US Grand Prix tie-ins plausible.
changed: Blackstone acquired a majority stake in a deal closed in 2025

name: La Doria
desc: Produces canned tomatoes, pasta sauces, pulses and fruit drinks, largely private-label for European supermarkets.
markets: Sells mainly to retailers in the UK, Italy, Germany and other European countries.
rationale: Private-label B2B food producer with no consumer brand to promote; weak F1 fit.
changed: Taken private by Investindustrial in 2022

name: Dutch Bros
desc: Drive-through coffee chain selling coffee, energy drinks, teas and smoothies through over 1,000 US shops.
markets: Shops in the US only, expanding eastward from the western states; no international plans.
rationale: Fast-growing US drive-through coffee brand; limited F1 fit outside the three US races.

name: San Miguel Corporation
desc: Philippine conglomerate with beer, spirits, food, packaging, power, fuel and infrastructure businesses including San Miguel Beer.
markets: Mainly the Philippines, with brewing and food operations in other South-East Asian markets and Hong Kong.
rationale: San Miguel Beer is a big regional brand with sports sponsorships; Singapore Grand Prix activation plausible.

name: Impossible Foods
desc: Makes plant-based meat products such as the Impossible Burger, sold through supermarkets and restaurant chains.
markets: Main market is the US, with sales in Canada, parts of Asia-Pacific and other markets.
rationale: Sustainability-led consumer brand; possible F1 sustainability tie-in but limited budget and plant-based niche.

name: Toast
desc: Provides cloud point-of-sale, payments, payroll and online ordering software for restaurants and hospitality businesses.
markets: Mainly US restaurants, with expansion into Canada, the UK and Ireland.
rationale: B2B fintech showcase possible via hospitality partners at US races; moderate F1 fit.

name: The Manitowoc Company
desc: Makes mobile, crawler and tower cranes under Grove, Manitowoc, National Crane and Potain brands for construction customers.
markets: Sells to contractors and rental firms in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Industrial B2B brand; F1 hospitality for dealers plausible but weak consumer fit.
changed: Spun off foodservice equipment business as Welbilt in 2016

name: Liquid Death
desc: Beverage brand selling canned still and sparkling water and iced tea with irreverent branding through retailers.
markets: Main market is the US, with retail sales in the UK.
rationale: Marketing-led youth brand known for irreverent sponsorships; F1 fan activation and content partnerships are plausible.

name: Cipriani
desc: Italian hospitality group running Cipriani restaurants, event venues, members' clubs and branded residences in major cities.
markets: Restaurants and venues in the US, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, including New York, London and Dubai.
rationale: Luxury hospitality brand suited to F1 Paddock Club, Monaco, Miami or Abu Dhabi hospitality.

name: Blank Street
desc: Coffee chain running small-format cafés selling espresso drinks and matcha at lower prices in big cities.
markets: Cafés in US cities such as New York, Boston and Washington, and in London.
rationale: Young urban coffee brand with limited budget; only small local activations in US or London plausible.

name: Thai Union Group
desc: Seafood company selling canned tuna brands John West, Chicken of the Sea and Petit Navire, plus pet food.
markets: Sells in over 100 countries, with major brands in Europe and North America.
rationale: Global consumer seafood brands; F1 tie-in plausible in European markets, moderate fit.

name: Eat Just
desc: Food technology company making JUST Egg plant-based egg products and Good Meat cultivated meat.
markets: Main market is the US, with sales in Asia and other markets.
rationale: Small sustainability-focused food technology brand with a limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit.
changed: Founded as Hampton Creek; later renamed

name: Cloetta
desc: Confectionery company making sweets, pastilles and chocolate under brands such as Läkerol, Malaco and Ahlgrens bilar.
markets: Main markets Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, the Netherlands, Germany and the UK.
rationale: Nordic confectionery brands with regional sales; limited F1 fit outside Nordic and Dutch activation.

name: Laird Superfood
desc: Plant-based food company selling coffee creamers, coffee, superfood powders and snacks through grocery and online channels.
markets: Customers mainly in the US through retailers and online; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Small niche US health-food brand with very limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit.

name: LifeMD
desc: Telehealth company offering virtual consultations and prescriptions for weight management, men's and women's health and primary care.
markets: Patients in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-only telehealth service; regulated health advertising limits what F1 marketing could achieve, weak fit.

name: Califia Farms
desc: Beverage company making plant-based milks, creamers and cold brew coffee sold through grocery retailers.
markets: Mainly US and Canada through grocery retailers; no verified wider expansion.
rationale: US premium plant-milk brand with a moderate marketing budget and no global reach; weak F1 fit.

name: Potbelly Sandwich Works
desc: Fast-casual sandwich chain serving toasted sandwiches, salads, soups and shakes in about 450 US shops.
markets: Shops in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-only restaurant chain now owned by a convenience-store group; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired by RaceTrac in 2025 and delisted from Nasdaq

name: Vita Coco
desc: Beverage company selling Vita Coco coconut water, coconut oil and other drinks through grocery and convenience retailers.
markets: Main market is the US, with sales in the UK and about 40 other countries.
rationale: Healthy hydration brand with sports marketing history; F1 fan and athlete activation plausible.

name: DailyPay
desc: Earned wage access platform letting employees of large employers draw earned pay before payday through an app.
markets: Employers and workers in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-focused B2B2C payroll fintech; limited F1 fit beyond hospitality for employer clients at US races.

name: Alera Group
desc: Insurance brokerage offering employee benefits, property and casualty, retirement and wealth services to US businesses and individuals.
markets: Clients in the US through local agencies; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US insurance broker with little national brand; client hospitality only, weak F1 fit.

name: HiBob
desc: Makes Bob, a cloud human resources platform for mid-size companies covering HR records, payroll, performance and compensation.
markets: Customers in the UK, US, Europe, Israel and Australia.
rationale: B2B software growing in the UK and US; F1 hospitality and brand awareness plausible.

name: TriNet
desc: Professional employer organisation providing outsourced payroll, benefits, HR and compliance services to small and mid-sized US businesses.
markets: Clients in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-focused B2B HR outsourcer serving small businesses; weak F1 fit beyond client hospitality.

name: Asure Software
desc: Provides cloud payroll, tax, time tracking and HR software for small and mid-sized US businesses.
markets: Customers in the US only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Small US payroll software vendor with a limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from Forgent Networks in 2007

name: Personio
desc: Provides cloud HR software covering recruiting, payroll, absence management and employee data for small and mid-sized companies.
markets: Customers mainly in Germany, the UK, Spain and other European countries.
rationale: European B2B software brand; F1 hospitality and awareness among European business buyers is plausible, moderate fit.

name: First Advantage
desc: Provides employment background screening, identity verification, drug testing and onboarding technology to employers.
markets: Mainly US employers, with operations in Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: B2B screening provider with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond client hospitality.
changed: Acquired Sterling Check in 2024
